overlay.panelHint: The status window floats above the game and shows whether the servers are fine — green when all systems are operational, amber with a countdown when maintenance is announced. Toggle it with the hotkey.
overlay.hotkeyTaken: This shortcut is not active: {{detail}}. Another program may own it — try a different key.
overlay.waylandHint: Global hotkeys cannot be registered on this desktop session. Bind this command to a key in your desktop settings instead:
overlay.pairHint: Pair with a server above — the window reads the service status through it.
overlay.kdeRuleInstalled: KDE window rule installed — overlays stay above the fullscreen game. (Written to ~/.config/kwinrulesrc; only windows titled "StarBuddy — " match.)
overlay.kdeRuleMissing: KDE stacks a focused fullscreen game above "keep above" windows. A window rule fixes that; StarBuddy adds it the first time an overlay opens.
overlay.sizeStrip: Always a strip while docked top or bottom

overlay.scanHint: Scan v2: F7 toggles a live reader that watches the signature area of the game frame (around the centre, a third down) and reads the amber signature badge with on-device OCR about once a second; the value is matched against the reference table and the window names the mineral (or cluster) and what the rock holds. "Scan now" reads one full frame. Models ≈ 15 MB, downloaded once. Screenshots never leave this machine.

scan.title: Scan
scan.idle: Press the scan hotkey on a scan result.
scan.privacy: Processed locally — the capture is kept in memory only.
scan.liveWaiting: Watching the signature area — ping a contact in scan mode.

match.unknown: No known mineral for this signature
match.groundHint: Ground deposits and debris carry only their size in the signature — the mineral follows from where you are.

overlay.captureHint: Sends the game window to StarBuddy for the training queue; contribute it from the Training page.

title.refinery: Drag across the refinery order panel
title.scan: Drag across the scan signature badge

need.refinery: Include the title bar: the station name is read from the "… REFINEMENT CENTER" line.
need.scan: Frame the badge only — the tighter the area, the more reliable the read.

region.hint: Escape keeps the area you had before.
region.saved: The orange box is the area in use now

refinery.title: Refinery order
refinery.empty: Press the refinery key with an order on screen.

overlay.readingHint: Off. Reading a refinery order, watching the scan badge and sending a training screenshot all need the game's window — switch this on and pick it once. The choice is remembered, so switching on again asks nothing, and the hotkey turns it on and off mid-flight. While it is on, your desktop shows that a window is being shared.
overlay.readingOn: On — reading {{source}}. Frames are read and dropped; nothing is stored and nothing leaves this machine unless you send it.
overlay.readingNeeded: These need screen reading switched on.
overlay.hotkeyPress: Hold the combination you want. Escape cancels.
overlay.hotkeyWindows: If a hotkey does nothing on Windows, StarBuddy also watches the keyboard directly, so a combination another program already owns still reaches it. If nothing arrives at all, the line above says so — and the usual cause left is keyboard software that remaps these keys for the game.
overlay.hotkeyDesktop: Your desktop delivers these hotkeys, so they work while the game has focus — and it has the last word on them: setting one here is a request, and the key you end up with is the one shown. They can also be changed under your desktop's own keyboard shortcut settings, listed as StarBuddy.
overlay.hotkeyDesktopUnset: Your desktop has taken these hotkeys over but has not put a key on any of them yet — until it does, they only work while a StarBuddy window has focus. Open your desktop's keyboard shortcut settings, find StarBuddy, and give each one a key. If it is not listed there, bind these commands to keys instead.
overlay.readingBorder: A yellow border round the game window is Windows saying the window is being captured. Windows 11 lets it be switched off and StarBuddy does; Windows 10 does not, and there it stays until reading is switched off.
overlay.hotkeyHeard: Last key received: {{action}}. The keys are reaching StarBuddy.
overlay.hotkeyNoneHeard_one: {{count}} shortcut registered, and no key has reached StarBuddy yet this session.
overlay.hotkeyNoneHeard_other: {{count}} shortcuts registered, and no key has reached StarBuddy yet this session.
overlay.readingBorderRefused: This machine refused StarBuddy borderless capture once, and Windows remembers the answer — which is why the border is there while other machines have none. Press System info below: it prints the registry key holding that answer. Delete the key, start StarBuddy again, and Windows will ask once more.
